author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China could face a substantially more capable Japanese military over the coming years as Tokyo considers nearly doubling its five-year defence spending to as much as 80 trillion yen (US$508 billion), according to media reports in Japan.
Observers said such a build-up could strengthen Japan’s ability to deter or respond to People’s Liberation Army operations around Taiwan and the East China Sea, as well as withstand attacks and sustain prolonged operations in a regional conflict.
The reported...
title: What’s the message for China as Japan weighs US$500 billion defence surge?

author: Nayan Seth,Lucy Quaggin
description:
Strong voter backlash in the US midterm elections against AI infrastructure projects, including data centres, indicates that framing the domestic buildout as key to competing with China failed to convince Americans and underscores the need to address local concerns, according to analysts.
“The argument that we need to build more data centres to win in AI against China no longer seems to have the kind of resonance it did before, if it ever did, frankly,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings...
title: Data centre dissent: why American voters aren’t buying Trump’s China AI pitch

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
US and Chinese defence officials met in Washington for the first meeting of a Crisis Communications and Prevention Working Group established under an agreement announced in September when leaders of the two nations met.
The two sides agreed on the importance of “advancing practical communication measures” to reduce risks between the US and China, according to a Pentagon readout of the meeting released Tuesday. Delegates also discussed “additional channels” to promote “effective” crisis...
title: China, US defence officials agree to improve ‘communication’ to reduce risks

author: Han Li
description:
Democrats scored a sweeping victory in Tuesday’s midterm elections, with Asian-Americans and other voters of colour playing a key role, according to a new voter poll released on Wednesday.
The 2026 Midterm Election Voter Poll surveyed 10,141 voters, including 2,130 Asian-American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) voters, between October 20 and November 3. It offers insights into voting trends across racial groups.
Taeku Lee, a Harvard professor of government and a researcher for the poll, said...
title: Asian-American voters, younger turnout fuel blue wave for Democrats in midterms

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
A Democratic victory that reached from Texas to Kansas changed the terms of Donald Trump’s final two years in office.
When the new US Congress convenes in January, Democrats will control both chambers. They can block his legislation, challenge spending on the war in Iran and scrutinise the deals he strikes with Beijing.
The day after his party lost control of Congress, Trump invited reporters to the construction site of his new White House ballroom to watch workers raise the final steel...
title: 5 takeaways from US midterms as Democrats sweep Congress and Trump faces Iran reckoning

author: Shi Huang
description:
No matter how thoroughly you brush your teeth in the morning and evening, the battle against bacteria is almost certain to be lost.
Within a few hours of brushing, it will return in force and rebuild a solid defence line on the surface of your teeth.
From ancient times to now, humanity has essentially had only one way of dealing with it, whether it was using twigs and sticks or the first bristled toothbrushes, which date back to 10th century China.
But even today’s most advanced electric brushes...
title: Chinese scientists make a toothbrush that uses mild electric shocks to reduce plaque

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
Republican Senator Susan Collins won in China on Tuesday. So did the volunteer firefighters.
Voters in several small American communities with China in their names cast ballots in Tuesday’s US midterm elections. Their local contests had little to do with Beijing and a great deal to do with fire engines, budgets and paving.
In China, a lakeside town in northeastern Maine, Collins outpolled Democrat Troy Jackson by 1,333 votes to 871, according to the town’s general election return. Statewide,...
title: Who won in China? In the US midterms, Susan Collins and the local firefighters

author: Han Li
description:
The incoming US Congress is set to include a record six lawmakers of Chinese descent after Democrat Richard Pan won a California House race.
Pan defeated incumbent Kevin Kiley in California’s 6th Congressional District by 15 percentage points, according to the latest results on Wednesday morning, adding another Chinese-American member to the House when the 120th Congress convenes in January.
“I’m proud to be part of the growing Asian-American representation in Congress,” Pan said in a statement...
title: US Congress welcomes record number of lawmakers of Chinese descent

author: Khushboo Razdan,Albee Zhang
description:
In the weeks leading up to the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump displayed unwavering confidence in his star power, urging supporters to close their eyes and “pretend I’m on the ballot”.
But Tuesday night’s disastrous results for the Republicans – the first time in 20 years both houses of Congress have changed hands at the same time – have punctured the aura of invincibility that once shielded Trump and allowed him to keep potential critics in line with the threat that opposing him...
title: Republicans face prospect of ‘civil war’ as Trump’s air of invincibility starts to fade

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
After almost two years in which the transatlantic alliance verged on collapse, a Democratic landslide in the US midterm elections was welcomed in Europe on Wednesday, even if few believed it would be a panacea for ailing ties.
The Democratic Party swept both chambers of the US Congress in a crushing rebuke of US President Donald Trump’s two-year record. For Europe, that period has led to a shattering of the post-war order and deep schisms in the Western coalition.
Trump has pulled US support for...
title: Bad to worse? Europe’s relief over US midterms tempered by prospect of Trump backlash

author: Fan Chen
description:
With just a fortnight until the Apec summit in Shenzhen, preparations are reportedly under way for the first meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the United States.
If the talks go ahead, they could bolster Beijing’s diplomatic standing, although the different priorities of each power were likely to limit consensus and yield few, if any, concrete concessions, observers said.
Officials from Beijing, Moscow, and Washington had been holding serious talks to arrange the first trilateral...
title: What is the one big thing that could stop Xi, Putin and Trump meeting at Apec?

author: Carol Yang
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here
In the wake of Democrats’ sweeping victory in congressional elections, Asian countries are weighing how their ties with the US will shift under a lame-duck Trump administration.
Observers expect the “blue wave” midterm results will push the Trump administration to heighten pressure on Washington’s Asian allies for greater US investment and increased defence cost-sharing.
In South Korea, analysts have predicted that managing relations with Washington will...
title: In Asia, midterms spark worries about diplomatic uncertainty, economic pressure

author: Dewey Sim
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here
Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, dealing a heavy blow to President Donald Trump as voters vented frustration over rising costs and the Iran war.
With Democrats set to take over Congress in January, they will have the power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate his administration.
Under these conditions, the president is expected to face a far more constrained final two years in office, with...
title: US midterm takeaways: Trump’s blame game, Elon’s space lasers and the rest of the world

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
Democrats won control of both houses of Congress in midterm elections as US voters punished President Donald Trump over inflation, corruption and rising healthcare costs.
The party was on track for at least 54 Senate seats after upset wins in long-standing Republican strongholds including South Carolina, Texas and Kansas. In the House of Representatives, Democrats were set to pick up dozens of seats and gain a double-figure majority.
A collapse in Trump’s approval ratings amid record petrol and...
title: Trump suffers midterms trouncing weeks before Xi meeting

author: Marco Vicenzino
description:
China is becoming increasingly important to the Gulf’s economic future. Yet the Gulf remains capable of disrupting China’s own.
That is the contradiction exposed by the US-Iran war. Beijing’s importance as an energy customer, investor and technology partner has grown, but its ability to guarantee the maritime routes connecting the Middle East to East Asia remains limited.
The next contest in global energy will concern not only who produces and consumes it, but who can preserve access when...
title: As US-Iran war shows, China’s influence can’t secure its line to Gulf oil

author: Amber Wang
description:
Taiwan expressed concern on Tuesday over more than 100 People’s Liberation Army naval vessels and mainland Chinese coastguard ships sailing across the western Pacific, including the Liaoning strike group conducting drills in the Philippine Sea.
The maritime deployment overlapped with a sharp spike in PLA aerial activity near the island. Taiwan’s defence ministry reported 49 sorties of PLA aircraft in the 24 hours to 6am on Tuesday, marking the highest single-day total this year. The number...
title: Taiwan flags massive PLA naval mobilisation, spike in air sorties

author: Eve Qiao
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here
Chinese social media users have voiced mixed views on the US midterm elections, criticising American politics while debating the implications of President Donald Trump’s political future for China.
Held on Tuesday, the midterm elections saw Democrats win control of both chambers of the US Congress, taking the House of Representatives and the Senate from the Republicans.
Democrats reached the 218-seat threshold needed for a House majority and also secured...
title: ‘Fake democracy’ or a plus for Beijing? Chinese internet users on the US midterms

author: Dewey Sim,Albee Zhang
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here
Beijing has vowed to continue working with Washington towards a “constructive relationship of strategic stability” following the Democrats’ sweeping victory in the US midterm elections on Wednesday.
But analysts said a Democratic-controlled US Congress would ramp up pressure on Beijing over Taiwan, artificial intelligence (AI) and export controls, though it might also eliminate uncertainties in negotiations.
When asked by reporters about the results on...
title: US midterm shift could squeeze China on AI, but bring clarity to bilateral talks

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here
In what appears to be an early attempt to distance himself from the Democrats’ historic gains, US President Donald Trump has sought to shift attention away from his party’s performance in the midterm elections, taking to social media to remind voters that he “wasn’t on the ballot”.
“I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump wrote as early results showed Democratic gains in places...
title: ‘I wasn’t on the ballot’: Trump deflects blame as Democrats on track to control Congress

author: Mark Magnier
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here
After weeks of insults, fearmongering and eye-popping spending on advertising, Americans settled down to vote on Tuesday, unleashing a blue wave that saw Democrats projected to take the House and the Senate, in a sharp rebuke to US President Donald Trump and his controversial governing style.
In a stunning development, Associated Press also projected that Democrat James Talarico won the Texas US Senate election, defeating Republican nominee Ken Paxton and...
title: US voters unleash blue wave, handing Congress to Democrats in rebuke to Trump

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here
For years, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) had little influence over the machinery of the Democratic Party. That is beginning to change.
The organisation has more than doubled its membership since 2024, reaching roughly 120,000, while growing numbers of DSA-backed candidates are positioning to expand its presence in Congress from two members to as many as seven.
The breakthrough came in New York, where Zohran Mamdani’s victory in the 2025 mayoral...
title: Frequently labelled as communists, who are the Democratic Socialists of America?

author: Dannie Peng
description:
The Tibetan Plateau, home to the world’s largest expanse of alpine permafrost, is warming at about twice the global average but, counter-intuitively,researchers have found that ice in parts of the Tibet autonomous region is actually thickening.
A team from Peking University found that shallow ground ice has unexpectedly increased over the past 20 years, affecting more than a third of the plateau’s permafrost, a phenomenon driven largely by natural climate factors.
The authors noted that the...
title: Chinese scientists discover thickening ground ice in parts of warming Tibet

author: Orange Wang
description:
Follow the SCMP’s live coverage here: High voter turnout as first US midterm results test Trump’s grip on Congress
The United States’ midterm elections are unlikely to deliver a “disruptive” shock to relations between Beijing and Washington despite potential volatility over the issue of Taiwan, according to a prominent Chinese expert in US studies.
Chen Dongxiao, president of the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said any shift in the make-up of the US Congress would mainly...
title: Will US midterm results lead to disruption in Washington’s ties with China?

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China is helping to train Solomon Islands police to use water cannons as part of an ongoing security partnership that is viewed with scepticism by the West.
The Chinese embassy said on Tuesday that six officers from the Royal Solomon Islands Police Force took part in a week-long training exercise, without giving dates.
The programme helped familiarise officers with the use of crowd control vehicles and different scenarios in which they may be used, the embassy said.
The programme cultivated a...
title: China training Solomon Islands police to use water cannons under security pact
